# Toggle

Toggle — turns one setting on or off, and the change takes effect at once. Controlled with `isChecked` or uncontrolled with `defaultChecked`. Built on Base UI's Switch: a `role="switch"` span with a hidden checkbox beside it for form submission. `readOnly` blocks the change at the root, so no hand-rolled click guard is needed. Extra attributes (`aria-label`, `aria-describedby`) go to the switch root.

Also asked as: enable disable, on/off setting.

**Import:** `import { Toggle } from '@/components';`

## Usage

Use a toggle to let a person turn something on or off instantly, such as making a resource public. If a physical switch would work for the action, a toggle is the right component.

A toggle never waits for a button. For an option that needs a button press to apply, such as a field in a form with a Save button, use a checkbox.

Pick the size by the page. Use 16 where the page has many toggles, such as a settings list. Use 20 to call attention to one setting, such as the single switch in a modal.

## Best practices

### Label what turns on. {#label-what-turns-on}

The label names the setting, not the switch position. It stays the same whether the toggle is on or off.

Do: The label names the setting.
Don't: "On" says nothing about what is on.

### Match the label to the state. {#match-the-label-to-the-state}

The switch and its label never disagree. A label that reads as a state, such as "Reminders on", is wrong the moment the switch is off; a noun phrase that names the setting, such as "Session reminders", reads right in both positions.

Do: Off, and the setting's name still reads right.
Don't: Off, but the label says on.

### Say why a toggle is disabled. {#say-why-a-toggle-is-disabled}

Disable a toggle only for something the person can fix on the same screen, and say why in text next to it. A setting a role can never use is hidden. Never put the reason in a tooltip on the disabled toggle.

Do: Disabled, with the reason beside it.
Don't: Disabled with no reason, so nothing says what to fix.

### The change lands at once. {#the-change-lands-at-once}

A toggle changes the setting as the person flips it. If the change needs confirming, saving or reviewing first, use a Checkbox in a form.

### Read-only is not disabled. {#read-only-is-not-disabled}

`isReadOnly` shows a setting the person may read but not change: the toggle stays in the tab order at full contrast, has no hover, says `aria-readonly` and ignores clicks. Say why beside it. `isDisabled` takes it out of the tab order and grays it, for a setting that does not apply right now.

### Name and id. {#name-and-id}

`name` is a form key, not an id; two toggles may share a name. `isChecked` controls the value and needs an `onChange`; `defaultChecked` sets the start.

### The role is a switch. {#the-role-is-a-switch}

The native input is a checkbox with `role="switch"`, the markup the W3C switch pattern ships. The platform maps the checked state, so no `aria-checked` is written. A `role` prop on the toggle replaces it.

## Accessibility

- **Label every toggle.** A visible `label` is better. Where the name sits elsewhere in the layout, pass `aria-label` so it still reaches assistive technology.
- **Do not change the label with the state.** The label stays the same whether the toggle is on or off.
- **Explain a disabled toggle.** Put the reason in visible text beside it, so a person who cannot reach it knows why. A disabled toggle leaves the tab order, and a tooltip on it is unreachable.
- **Keyboard focus is a 2px ring on `border.focused`, 2px off the track.** Space flips the toggle.

## Related

- For an option that needs a button press to apply, use Checkbox.
- To choose one option from a visible set, use Radio.
- To choose one option from a longer list, use Select.
- To explain what flipping a toggle does, add a Tooltip.

## Parts

1. **Track.** A pill, 32 by 16 or 40 by 20. Off it is the neutral bold fill; on it is the selected bold fill.
2. **Thumb.** An inverse circle inset 2 from the track. It slides to the end when the toggle is on.
3. **Label.** 14/20 text beside the track in a 24 row. It names the setting and stays the same in both states.
4. **Spinner.** Optional, between the track and the label while a change is saved.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Off: `--ds-background-neutral-bold`. On: `--ds-background-selected-bold`. |
| Hovered | Off: `--ds-background-neutral-bold-hovered`. On: `--ds-background-selected-bold-hovered`. |
| Pressed | No step of its own. The hovered fill holds while the pointer is down. |
| Focused | A 2px ring in `--ds-border-focused`, 2px off the track, for keyboard focus only. |
| Disabled | `--ds-background-disabled` track, `--ds-icon-disabled` thumb, in both positions. Out of the tab order. |
| Read-only | Full contrast, in the tab order, no hover, `aria-readonly`. Not changeable. |
| Loading | A spinner sits between the track and the label; input is ignored. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Track size | `--toggle-track-height-16` and `--toggle-track-width-16`; `-20` for the large size. |
| Thumb inset | `--toggle-pad`. |
| Track fill | `--ds-background-neutral-bold` off; `--ds-background-selected-bold` on. |
| Thumb | `--ds-icon-inverse`; `--ds-icon-disabled` when disabled. |
| Row | `--item-height-sm`; gap `--stack-md`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name the setting as a noun phrase: "Session reminders". | An instruction or a status: "Turn on reminders", "Reminders are on". |
| Use sentence case and no end punctuation. | Title case, or a period after the label. |
| Keep the label to a few words. | A sentence that explains the setting. Put the explanation in a caption or a Tooltip. |
| Write the label so it reads right in both positions. | "Enable" or "Disable" in the label, which the position already says. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | Id of the switch, which the label points at. A generated id is used when omitted. |
| `name` | string | — | Form key sent with the hidden checkbox and reported in `onChange`. |
| `label` | node | — | Visible text beside the track. Where the label sits elsewhere, leave it out and pass `aria-label`. |
| `value` | string or number | `'on'` | Form value sent when the toggle is on, and reported as `target.value` in `onChange`. Defaults to `on`. |
| `isChecked` | bool | — | Controlled on or off state. Pair it with `onChange`; when it is set, `defaultChecked` is ignored. |
| `defaultChecked` | bool | — | Starting state of an uncontrolled toggle. |
| `size` | enum | `16` | Track height in pixels: `16` (default) or `20`. |
| `isDisabled` | bool | `false` | Prevents interaction and dims the toggle. |
| `isLoading` | bool | `false` | Shows a spinner while a change is being saved and ignores input. |
| `isReadOnly` | bool | `false` | Shows the state without letting the user switch it. |
| `onChange` | func | — | Called with `{ target: { name, value, checked } }` when the user switches it. Not called while the toggle is read-only or loading. |
| `onFocus` | func | — | Called with the focus event when the switch gains focus. |
| `onBlur` | func | — | Called with the blur event when the switch loses focus. |
| `onClick` | func | — | Called with the click event on the switch. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class on the wrapper around the track and label. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline style on the wrapper around the track and label. |
| `testId` | string | — | Maps to `data-testid`, for test queries. |

## Variants

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.
